references.text: The Lord reveals Himself to Moses and proclaims His grace and mercy, stating that He forgives iniquity, transgression, and sin. Moses' prayer in Num 14:19 is built on this revelation of God's character.
Moses asks God to forgive the people's sin after the incident with the golden calf. This shows a similar pattern where Moses intercedes for Israel's sin.
The psalm praises the Lord's mercy and grace (חֶסֶד), and how He forgives all iniquity. This reflects Moses' appeal to God's great grace.
The psalm describes how God saved Israel from Egypt and showed them grace despite their rebellion, which corresponds to Moses' reference to God's faithfulness from Egypt onward.
Describes how God, in His mercy, forgave iniquity and did not destroy the people. This reflects Moses' prayer for forgiveness based on God's grace.
Nehemiah reminds us that God is a God of forgiveness, gracious and merciful, slow to anger and rich in love, and that He did not abandon the people. This echoes Moses' prayer in the wilderness.
Micah praises God who forgives iniquity and bears with sin, and who delights in showing grace (חֶסֶד). This reflects Moses' appeal to God's great grace.
The Lord's answer to Moses' prayer where He says that He has forgiven as Moses asked. This is the direct fulfillment of the prayer in verse 19.
Moses recounts his intercession for the people and asks God not to destroy His people whom He saved from Egypt. Similar themes of intercession and reference to the exodus from Egypt.
